entities.name: Antiochus of Ascalon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antiochus of Ascalon was a prominent 1st-century BC Platonist philosopher who played a significant role in the development of Middle Platonism.

Born in the Greek city of Ascalon, Antiochus rejected skepticism and blended Stoic doctrines with Platonism, creating a unique philosophical system that had a lasting impact on Western thought.

His teachings, which emphasized the importance of reason and the pursuit of knowledge, attracted a large following and influenced prominent philosophers such as Cicero and Quintus Smyrnaeus.

Despite his significant contributions to philosophy, Antiochus' life was cut short when he was murdered in 67 BCE, leaving behind a legacy that continued to shape Western philosophy for centuries to come.

The Antiochene School, which he founded, became a major center of philosophical learning, attracting scholars from across the ancient world.

Today, Antiochus of Ascalon is remembered as a key figure in the history of philosophy, whose work continues to be studied and debated by scholars around the world.

The inscription on his tombstone, which reads 'I am Antiochus, son of Ascalon, a Platonist', serves as a poignant reminder of his enduring legacy.
